marketing_architecture_body: Everything deploys as a single Cloudflare Worker: the app, the API, auth, jobs, crons, and workflows. One deploy, one log stream, and no service mesh between you and production. Cloudflare's primitives replace the usual fleet of services.
marketing_binding_crons_detail: Scheduled jobs, registered in code and merged into the deploy.
marketing_binding_d1_detail: Relational data behind a typed Drizzle schema.
marketing_binding_do_detail: Realtime rooms, presence, notifications, and the AI agent.
marketing_binding_queues_detail: Typed background jobs with a dead-letter queue.
marketing_binding_r2_detail: File storage for uploads, served straight from the Worker.
marketing_binding_workflows_detail: Durable multi-step processes that survive restarts.
marketing_blog_lede: Architecture decisions, Cloudflare patterns, and what shipping on a typed foundation actually looks like.
marketing_blog_seo_description: Notes from building Onyx: architecture decisions, Cloudflare patterns, and what shipping on a typed foundation actually looks like.
marketing_changelog_lede: Onyx is the foundation JXD builds on, so it improves whenever the work does. Every drop lands here.
marketing_changelog_seo_description: Every Onyx release: what shipped and when. The foundation improves continuously.
marketing_contact_lede: No forms, no queues. Questions about Onyx, licensing, or an engagement all land in the same place.
marketing_contact_reason_broken_detail: License holders get fixes fast. Include what you expected and what happened instead.
marketing_contact_reason_built_detail: JXD ships products on Onyx in weeks, with a full handover at the end.
marketing_contact_reason_buy_detail: Licensing questions, invoicing, or whether your use fits. Ask before you buy.
marketing_contact_seo_description: Questions about Onyx, licensing, or having JXD build your product. One email reaches the engineer.
marketing_cta_body: Start at the interesting part. Get the foundation, keep the repository, and ship your product on it.
marketing_dev_body: Local dev simulates the whole platform: the database, storage, queues, Durable Objects, cron triggers, and workflows all run on your machine with no cloud account. Foundations only stay healthy where they can be exercised.
marketing_dev_loop_note: D1, R2, Queues, DOs, crons, and workflows, simulated locally
marketing_dev_testing_body: Playwright covers the real journeys, Vitest covers the units, and CI enforces types, tests, and bundle-size budgets on every push.
marketing_engagement_description: JXD builds your product on Onyx.
marketing_faq_agents_detail: Yes, deliberately. Focused packages, per-package READMEs, a maintained CLAUDE.md, and typed contracts give agents the structure they need to make correct changes.
marketing_faq_agents_term: Does it work with AI coding agents?
marketing_faq_cloudflare_detail: Not to build. Local dev simulates D1, R2, Queues, Durable Objects, crons, and workflows. You need an account when you deploy, and the free tier goes a long way.
marketing_faq_cloudflare_term: Do I need a Cloudflare account?
marketing_faq_contents_detail: The complete repository: the application, the docs site, every package, the Playwright and Vitest suites, and the CI pipeline. It runs locally with one command.
marketing_faq_license_detail: One purchase covers one product. The full terms come with the purchase; if you are unsure whether your use fits, ask {email}.
marketing_faq_lockin_detail: Onyx is Cloudflare by default, portable by design. Capabilities live in focused packages behind small interfaces, so swapping the storage, database, or deploy target is contained work, not a rewrite.
marketing_faq_updates_detail: Onyx is the foundation JXD builds client products on, so it improves continuously. The changelog tracks every drop, and because you own the fork, you pull what you want when you want it.
